question: Does geometry-informed candidate selection improve on pose selection under a matched output/candidate/NMS budget?
key_result: Existing matched-output/matched-NMS comparisons differ in effective candidate count14/20; the minimum missing comparison is pose-nearest14 plus unchanged NMS against original geometry14 plus NMS.

skills_applied.scope: Evaluation framework, variable control and baseline fairness only

analysis_metadata.role: Retrospective evidence audit after S11, not a preregistered experiment or independent performance replication.

existing_numerical_analysis.scope: Already saved support and selection records only; no new selection or scoring.

pose14_prerequisites.scope: Saved JSON field/rank/tie audit only. No candidate14 pool or new selected IDs generated, no NPZ opened, no selector/renderer run.

minimum_missing_experiment.new_policy: pose-nearest14 from same eligible20; original pose ranking and NMS to4
minimum_missing_experiment.same: query/input information, candidate count14, output4, pose metric/precision, NMS threshold/relaxation/fallback, evaluation mask
minimum_missing_experiment.different: candidate formation criterion and hence permitted candidate identities
minimum_missing_experiment.GT_oracle_priority: not part of the minimal missing comparison

limitations: All inputs/results already seen; no unseen generalization or independence implied.
Support is measured depth-consistency union over valid query points, not generated video quality.
GT scoring is separate from selection but query/history observations are statistically related.
Full20 step traces do not contain a complete pair-distance matrix.
Same-candidate identities plus the same downstream ranking/NMS remove any route for current geometry weights to change the output.
